chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, from Suleiman ibn Abbad, from Isa ibn Abu al-Ward, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).

That the Children of Israel complained to Musa (peace be upon him) about the whiteness (vitiligo) they were experiencing, so he took that complaint to Allah, Glorious and High. So Allah revealed to him: 'Order them to eat the meat of the cow with the chard (salt/celery greens).'

key_terms.السِّلْقِ: Chard or salt (a specific vegetable or seasoning used as remedy)

ai.seo_question: What was the remedy for the Children of Israel's skin disease according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* links the biblical narrative of the Cow (Surah Al-Baqarah) to a specific medicinal remedy, interpreting 'al-silq' as chard or a similar green vegetable to treat vitiligo. Shia scholars often cite this to demonstrate the continuity of divine guidance and the practical application of Quranic injunctions in healing, emphasizing that the command was not merely ritualistic but had tangible health benefits for the Israelites.
